hypothesis: If the claim holds, GBIF records of native (non-introduced) amphibians will be essentially absent from truly oceanic islands, meaning those never connected to a continent.
pass_criterion: Of a pre-listed set of at least 30 oceanic islands or archipelagos (for example Hawaii, Azores, Galapagos, Canaries, Mascarenes, St Helena, Ascension, Tristan da Cunha, Kerguelen, Bermuda, Cape Verde), at least 95% have zero amphibian occurrences with establishmentMeans = NATIVE after excluding records known to be introduced.
fail_criterion: More than 10% of the listed oceanic islands have at least one native amphibian species supported by a verified native occurrence.
interpretation: 'Batrachians' means Amphibia (Anura, Caudata, plus Gymnophiona if present). 'Oceanic islands' means islands of volcanic or coral origin that were never joined to a continent, so continental fragments such as Seychelles, New Zealand and Madagascar are excluded. GBIF establishmentMeans and island/country fields allow introduced frogs to be separated from native ones.

dataset.name: GBIF Occurrence Download / Occurrence API (class Amphibia)
dataset.why_it_fits: Fields used: taxonKey (Amphibia), island, countryCode, decimalLatitude, decimalLongitude, establishmentMeans, basisOfRecord. Each download gets its own DOI when generated.
